review_notes: I read the whole file. It has no @[simp] declarations, no simp-set or simp-attribute manipulation, and no custom definitions that would need normal-form lemmas. All the theorems are helper lemmas with hypothesis-heavy statements about ideal membership. They are used by explicit application, not as rewrite rules. The `simp` calls are `simp [f]`, `simp only [Ideal.mem_comap, mem_nilradical]`, `simpa [map_mul, map_sub, AlgHom.commutes]` and `simp only [map_sub]; ring`. All are local and closed. None of them suggests a missing canonical simp lemma, a wrongly oriented rewrite, competing rules or a cycle. Tagging `map_mul_self_sub_mem_span` or `map_mem_map_maximalIdeal` as simp would be unjustified: they carry a hypothesis and their conclusions are not canonical forms. I did not search Mathlib for overlapping lemmas, because there was no simp-interface claim to check. I could not run Lean, so I make no claim about simplifier behaviour beyond reading the source.
